title: Predatory
body:
1. They create an unnecessary sense of urgency to get consumers to make unsound purchasing decisions. I was bombarded with notifications with a measly time-limited discount (sometimes less than $1) for almost every item once you start “liking” things. These are on by default and I’m not sure you can turn them off at all. This is clearly done to get users out of a “browsing” mindset and push us into purchasing, using invasive psychology, with a disregard for the right to make decisions without being pressured.

2. There is also a spotlighted section of items that were already sold in the same notification tab. I was made to feel like I missed out of things I had already made a connection with, even though I never would’ve thought twice about them if not for this feature. This to me seals the deal on creating that sense of urgency whenever the platform is used: making it feel like there are bigger stakes than there actually are through the psychologically manipulative design decisions.

3. It’s very clear they make more money from app than website users (laptop screens make purchases feel like they require more responsibility so make people harder to manipulate). Instead of respecting this disparity, they seem to do everything in their power to push users toward the app. Certain key features (like reporting posts or even a ‘delete account’ button) are only available in the app, despite there being no reason to be unable to provide them on a website from a technical perspective. 

4. Amazon resellers and dropshippers run rampant, especially in the jewelry section. If you do use this platform (which I don’t recommend), PLEASE at least put in a few key words into the Amazon search bar before buying anything. Especially when items are sold without a tag or identifying info; even more so when they’re sold in “sets” or you see multiple identical/similar listings. You will often find full packs for cheaper than the few resold items from them are listed for; you will often find an identical item for cheaper on Walmart/Amazon. (Reverse image searching doesn’t always work because many sellers buy the item first and take their own photos).

5. On a more personal note: I ask you to imagine a bunch of people sitting in a meeting discussing all these predatory tactics as impersonal “strategies,” talking about us like we’re numbers, because their biggest commitment is to maximizing their own profits and they don’t even see us as people because of it. It doesn’t matter to them that the site is unusable from listings that violate their guidelines because they are still making money. It doesn’t matter to them that we are making unwise decisions because they are still making money. And in fact, as long as these things do make them more money, they’re considered successes no matter how they affect us.

Thanks for reading this if you did. I highly recommend staying away from this app.

I was ready to give a five star!  Then an ad popped up. No biggie!  Right?

Wrong!

I hate that.  For that reason alone I’m removing the app and no longer interested in this company’s other budget apps I sorely need.

I guess I’ll have to pay the big bucks for a quicken program or something.

I HATE FORCED ADS!

For me it really hurts a company’s ability to showcase a reasonably priced product.

No I won’t pay for a phone app until I know I like it and it works!

I was ready to buy and check out other products.

Give me a way to close out of an ad and I will be willing to pay to get rid of ads altogether.

But when I’m forced to watch. Deal breaker.

I pay extra to stream ad free.  I at least get to see what I’m streaming before I’m forced to make a decision.

There is only one thing I would change to up my rating to a 5 star rating- I wish when I clicked on each category, say I click on Groceries in the Categories section, I wish it pulled up every transaction that I’ve placed in that category instead of just the options to edit the title and icon! title: Sellers Beware
body:
First let me say, Selling items on VINTED is super easy. Now let me warn sellers. I was denied compensation for an item getting damaged while in transit through the USPS. This is the message I received from HAMZA …                                                    
“Thanks for reaching out to us! After reviewing the case, we couldn’t confirm that the damage was caused by the carrier. The available infor shows that the parcel either wasn’t damaged in transit or the packaging wasn’t sufficient to protect the item.
Because of this, we can’t issue compensation in this case.
Thank you for your understanding.”
**My response**There is no proof USPS damaged it in transit (why would they say they damaged it) So based on that reason alone, I MUST not have packed the item properly. I wrapped the item in bubble wrap then put it inside a shipping package then put it in the box. I uploaded the pictures of the Damaged box , then I took a picture of the shipping package where you see that my broken item is wrapped in bubble wrap. Another point I would like to add, if they looked at the tracking info it shows my item is still sitting somewhere since Aug 25,2026. I could have kept my mouth shut & just wait til 2 days after Sept 25,2026 for a refund (per VINTEDs policy) but I didn’t do that. Maybe just maybe VINTED should allow more than 5 pictures. I feel since they couldn’t really prove either scenario regarding damage - I didn’t expect the Full amount but Good customer service would have been to offer something.  So *Seller Beware*

title: Best selling app BUT
body:
I’ve sold a lot on this platform and overall enjoy using it, especially the offer process. However, there are a few areas that could really be improved.

One of my biggest frustrations is the limited options for canceling orders. I’ve had two orders where buyers changed their minds but refused to cancel the orders themselves, leaving me to do it. As a result, the cancellations negatively affected my seller account, even though neither situation was my fault. In one case, the buyer simply changed their mind. In the other, the buyer didn’t fully review the listing photos before purchasing. There should be an option to specify the reason for a cancellation so sellers aren’t get penalized when the buyer is responsible.

Another issue is the payout process. I’m referring to the initial payout after an order is marked as complete. Once the app shows that the buyer has received the item and the transaction is complete, the funds should be reflected in my account promptly. Instead, sometimes they appear quickly, while other times it takes several days for the balance to update. A more consistent and predictable timeline would make the process much less frustrating.

Finally, the app’s message notifications need attention. I frequently receive notifications indicating I have unread messages when I don’t. Right now, for example, the app says I have eight unread messages, but there aren’t any new messages to open. I’ve tried deleting conversations, reopening messages, and refreshing the app to clear the notifications. Sometimes it works, but most of the time it doesn’t. This has happened repeatedly and has become very frustrating.

I’m constantly having items restricted even though they don’t appear on the list of restricted items. At the same time, I purchased items listed as “new in box” that arrived used.

When I tried to report the issue, I had to go through a lengthy process. I had to wait for the seller to review the order and approve the return, only for the seller to claim that I was the one who had opened the item. The entire experience was exhausting, and I never felt like I was able to speak with a real person.

The inconsistent enforcement and lack of accessible customer support have been extremely frustrating.

title: Best habit app you will find!
body:
I’ve genuinely tried all the habit apps- simple ones, complex ones, gamified ones, expensive ones — and HabitKit is easily the best of the bunch.

The grid based visual tracking is brilliant. It’s simple, motivating, and incredibly satisfying to look at. No unnecessary fluff, no overwhelming features- just a beautifully designed system that actually makes you want to stay consistent.

Customization is excellent, the UI is clean and intuitive, and it strikes the perfect balance between powerful and easy to use. This is the first habit app I’ve stuck with long term.

If you’re serious about building habits (or breaking bad ones), stop searching. HabitKit is it.

title: The Perfect App For What I Needed
body:
This app on my phone has been insanely helpful and so easy to use. I can track anything going on in my life and then easily look back over the history of my habit. Things like how frequently I’m vacuuming or if I took my medication each day or week. Every time I login and track my habits it also reminds me of things I might not have done yet like…oh I haven’t done that thing yet today. So I often get up to start or finish something because I see that it isn’t checked off for the day. 

What makes this app better than others I was looking at is that I’m 100% choosing my own categories and specific tasks. So my weird and wonderful lists are tailored perfectly to me, and there isn’t anything extraneous. 

The only complaint I have is that the data is only on your device. So I can see and use it on my phone but I can’t pull it up on my tablet or computer. I reached out to the developers and they say they hope to change this in the future. So fingers crossed, this app could get even better.
author: Hattrik103

title: Almost perfect - Few updates needed
body: I first downloaded HabitKit in the ending of March 2025. I bought the lifetime premium version. When I first downloaded the app, it didn't have an option for putting your own emojis for habits, which was really frustrating. I'm very happy that they finally put an emoji update. I was tired of using a dog bone for my seafood habit. My issue with the new update is that you can't change the skin color of the emojis. It's also disappointing that you can't choose a set of Crayola like colors for your habits including brown, instead of the preset pastel colors that is given. No true red or solid purples just a pastel palette for everything... I also think that the counter for 1, 5, 10 , 15 shouldn't be there. I think that instead the only option should be to set your own number of "Pages read" for each habit. It would look much better for the eyes that way. Or at least give the option to turn it off and only have your own preset number. I also think that the HabitKit wrapped should be worded better and upgraded. Besides those things, this is a decent app for habit tracking. I do also believe having a bad habit tracker section or page would be great, and helpful for separation of good and bad habits. Plus not being able to sync to iCloud is hella wack. I can only give 2 stars because I know it could be better.

title: Best tracker out there
body:
Hands down one of the best habit trackers that I’ve found out there. The user interface is very intuitive and easy to use. It has absolutely everything I was looking for.
1. Ability to set daily, weekly or monthly goals.
2. Ability to create a goal that requires multiple completions to count toward a streak (i.e. taking meds—you can create two instances that go toward one goal).
3. Reminders that you can create to help you remember to complete your goal. Let’s face it some of us get busy and lose track of things we want to do during the day and this helps immensely.

These functions are in the pro version which is completely worth it, without a doubt.

body: I love this app for tracking my habits! I’ve tried other apps and none of them were as good as this one. I can track as many habits as I want to, and I can archive them when I want to stop tracking them (but it doesn’t delete them so I can “unarchive”them if I want to start tracking that habit again. I would like to suggest a couple of things that I think could make it better…first, I’d love to be able to set an alarm for my habits to remind me to do some of them. I’d also like to have a bigger color selection to choose from. The colors it has are beautiful and vibrant but I’d just like to add some more shades (because I track a lot of habits). I love the icons too, and the fact that I can reorder my habits at any time. All in all, it’s a fantastic app and I use it everyday! title: Limited formatting options and never syncs on macOS
body:
A journal is just yet another type of word-processing app. Presentation probably isn’t the highest priority, but this app only supports a minimum set of formatting options. It would be nice to have headings, sub-headings, etc. to structure the various topics  that one might want to journal.

However, my biggest gripe is that, while I can create and edit entries on my iPhone and iPad Mini, nothing ever shows up on my MacBook Pro. (To be clear, the iCloud setting to store Journal data on iCloud is setup on all of my devices.

Entering detailed journal entries using an iPhone or iPad screen keyboard is horrific, and prevents me getting my thoughts down easily. It would be so much nicer to be able to do that with my Mac.

title: Unreliable and hard to use
body:
I really wanted to like this app, but it ended up being frustrating and unreliable.

First, organizing notes is a mess. There’s no clear or effective way to categorize recordings, separate meetings, or keep projects distinct. If you record frequently, everything quickly turns into an unmanageable pile.

The meeting summary and output features sound great in theory, but they don’t consistently work. I’ve had recordings sit there indefinitely without generating a summary. In one case, I had to wait until the next day and try again — and because of that delay, I ended up paying for an extra week of the subscription just to access notes that should have been available earlier.

Exporting is another major pain point. There’s no bulk export option, so you have to download files one by one. On top of that, the file formats are inconsistent — some export as MP3, others as M4A — which creates extra work if you need them in a uniform format.

Transcription is also unreliable. The app claims to auto-generate transcripts, but sometimes timestamps are included and sometimes they aren’t. For meeting notes and professional use, timestamps are pretty standard and often necessary, so this inconsistency makes the transcripts less useful.

Overall, the app has promising ideas but poor execution. Between the organizational issues, unreliable summaries, inconsistent exports, and unpredictable transcripts, it just wasn’t worth the subscription. I canceled.

title: Fundamental Reliability Problems
body:
At the most fundamental level, a voice notes app needs to record and trust, once lost, is hard to gain back.

In just two weeks of testing Voicenotes, I've lost approximately three hours of very important recordings.

First incident (March 11, iPhone): I was recording a note that reached 54 minutes when I paused it. I checked back twice over the next 25 minutes and the paused recording was still there both times. When I went to resume it the third time (roughly 30mins after pausing), it had vanished completely. The company acknowledged this as an "edge case."

Second incident (March 25, Mac laptop): I recorded a critical 2-hour meeting on my Mac laptop. The laptop remained on and active throughout. When the meeting ended, I pressed stop and clicked the arrow key in the Mac app (that takes you the dashboard/site). The recording disappeared and I couldn't find it anywhere.

Apple Watch reliability issues: Recording on the Apple Watch never worked consistently. Recordings would stop abruptly and disappear into the ether. I didn't even report this because I gave up on that feature rather quickly.

If one user can encounter two "edge cases" in about two weeks, this app is not for me. I can't trust an app that loses important content, especially when those conversations can't be recreated. Three hours of critical recordings is too much to lose.

To potential users: If you're recording important content you can't afford to lose, I'd recommend testing thoroughly with non-critical recordings first, or considering more established alternatives.

To the developer: The core functionality needs to be rock solid before adding features. Focus on ensuring recordings are reliably saved across all platforms.

I'll be looking for other options.

title: Dietary Restrictions/Requirements.
body:
1.  It only lets you select one dietary restriction. What if you need gluten free and vegetarian?    Said select all that apply but only allowed me to select one.  
2. What if you only have one person with a dietary restriction?  If you select vegetarian, gluten free, ect it assumes all meals must be 100% that dietary requirement. In my house we have 1 vegetarian and 3 carnivores so this app isn’t much help. I have to plan 2 meal plans. What I would like is something that plans a meal plan for the entire family.  If 1 of 4 is vegetarian have a meal plan with a meat entree, a vegetarian entree that could double as a side, a 2nd vegetable side and a whatever else is in the plan for that meal. To do this though the app needs to ask how many of the family members have the dietary restrictions, then plans meals that can fit. 
It seems the app would be pretty good for those with households that don’t need more than 1 dietary restriction or mixed dietary requirements.

title: More frustrating than beneficial.
body:
Technical Issues:
1) When trying to chat with the AI bot thing (which I feel like nowadays there’s an over-reliance on these chat bots anyway and they often can’t resolve things because they’re, respectfully, too dumb to understand what’s being asked or said) after you hit submit the app instantly crashes.

2) When trying to complete grammar exercises, you reach the end and it says to practice more and then it throws an internet connection error. I’m on cellular and nothing has changed soooo?


Learning Issues

1) there’s a fundamental disconnect with how people learn and retain information. And I know everyone’s different but it’s not helpful or beneficial for you to say nope that’s not it, try again and let me keep trying especially if it’s fill in the blank. If I’m drawing a blank continually guessing is only going to create frustration. You would think if you worked with educators to design this app you employ psychology that works in a classroom setting to improve learning and retention but that’s noticeably absent here. 

2) same concept, but when you miss answers explaining the WHY versus nope that’s not it, try again, would before beneficial than having me continually guess. If someone’s missing multiple questions within the same exercise there’s an obvious disconnect of something not being understood and the app just ignores that and moves in a forward direction. They’ll say oh we have reviews but if you’re asking me after I just missed something and I’ve seen the right answer, I can get it right but does that mean I understand WHY it’s right or wrong or is that just good memory recall? 

3) on listening exercises (in Spanish) they speak entirely too fast for a beginners course and you have people that dont annunciate well so it literally sounds like they’re slurring whole sections of words and sentences together and then you’re presented this blank field to type what you heard and it’s like I heard a blob of ran together words. Again not helpful to someone trying to learn from scratch.

title: Lacks features of free software

It also conditionally lets you review vocab using flash cards, speaking, or typing. Why am I only allowed to do that sometimes? I can’t always speak aloud to practice. I guess they are taking their name Babble literally. It’s pretty bare bones visually as well. 

The positive is I’m not learning to translate weird sentences I’ll never use like in Duolingo, I’m not forced to watch ads, and restricted to “energy” or hearts. Also a year is less than that of Duolingo so that’s a plus too. 

It gets the job done but I expected more out of the gate from a paid app.

title: Issue Summary
body:
Issue Summary:
I noticed a problem in how Focus Keeper calculates focus time during a Pomodoro cycle.
Today, I completed the first session normally. In the second session, I had 7 minutes left but had to stop and leave the app from morning until late at night. When I came back at night, I finished the remaining 7 minutes, then completed sessions 3 and 4.
My real focus time for the day was 100 minutes.
However, the Achievements page counted the long break (from morning to night) as if it were focus time, and showed more than 10 hours of focus.
Expected behavior: The app should count only the actual minutes spent focusing, even if a session is paused for many hours.
Actual behavior: When a session is paused for a long time, the app adds the entire real-world gap to the focus total, which makes the daily focus time incorrect.
Please fix this issue so the focus time reflects actual work time only.

title: Lacks various basic pieces of functionality (just like every other Google mobile app)
body:
Have you ever wanted to do something relatively straightforward, such as subscribing to a Google Calendar calendar from the Apple Calendar app (or vice versa) on your mobile device? I sure have. Surely I can simply do that using the Google Calendar app, right?

Nope, sorry. They couldn't be bothered to put features like that into their app.

"To subscribe to a new calendar, you must use a computer web browser. You can't subscribe to a calendar in the Google Calendar app for Android, iPhone, or iPad."

This isn't the only feature that's inexplicably missing, but it's a good representative summary of my experience using the Google Calendar app (and the Gmail app, and the Docs app, and the Sheets app, and pretty much every Google mobile app).

Do you want to do things that are basic features of the Google product you're using? Do you have a reasonable expectation that the mobile app would offer a first-class experience that would allow you to do those things? Well, too bad. Anything beyond the most rudimentary feature set is left out of the mobile apps, and that's apparently what they want the experience to be.

The thing is, smartphones and tablets aren't toys. People expect to be able to do sophisticated things with them. Teams of developers at Google created and maintain native apps for their products, which represents a non-trivial amount of effort. Yet they just kinda couldn't be bothered to put in features that they reckon they could get away with leaving out. (Even as they increasingly shove "AI" features into the very same mobile apps.)

"Sorry, we just kinda couldn't be bothered, so go open a web browser on a PC and do it over there instead" might have been forgivable back in 2007, but it's not 2007. In the intervening two decades, I would have expected Google to eventually figure out that yes, actually, people *do* want to be able to use all of the features of Google products when using the associated native app on their $1000 tablet docked to a keyboard.

For the true Google Calendar experience, delete the app off your device and instead exclusively access it awkwardly via the web interface in Mobile Safari, as Steve Jobs intended, like it's iPhoneOS 1.0.

title: A model for all other apps!
body:
When I found out there was a phone version of Procreate I said, “take my money!” Now, instead of playing a game or surfing social media when I’m bored or waiting, I doodle, draw and create. 

I wrote this review after Pocket kept crashing when I chose the adjustments tool. I came to the App Store to see if there was an update, and lo and behold, it had been published just 30 minutes earlier! Problem solved. Thank you developers!

Here’s what I absolutely love about the app: 
- Pay once and it’s yours. No upgrades, premium features or in-app purchases.
- No annoying subscriptions. 
- Zero ads, not even for games or brushes or other “upgrades.”
- It works as you’d expect as a Procreate user. Use layers, alpha lock, masking, drawing assist, symmetry, advanced mesh, etc.  
- The brush set is decent but you can add new or make your own. I made a monoline brush because the app surprisingly didn’t have one. I’ve never made a brush before but it was easy with a bit of trial and error! (I started with the hard airbrush and tweaked from there.) and it’s exactly what I need. 
- you can zoom in almost infinitely to create fairly detailed art with just a fat finger and a LOT of erasing, lol. Seriously… I made a phone screen-size canvas and put 15 small “frames” on it so I could practice color theory and speed art.  If only Apple made a phone that works with the pencil…

That pretty much sums up the app.

title: Serious Memory Leak in the macOS Packet Tunnel
body:
Shadowrocket 2.2.90 has a serious memory leak in its macOS Network Extension. After 11 days of continuous operation, the MacPacketTunnel process grew to a 5.68 GB memory footprint with more than 12.3 million heap allocations. Approximately 5 GB had been pushed into swap, causing severe system lag on a 16 GB Intel iMac running macOS 26.5.2.

The problem was not caused by network buffers: they occupied only 224 KB. Almost all the accumulated memory was in MALLOC_SMALL and MALLOC_TINY.

Quitting and reopening the Shadowrocket interface did not restart the tunnel extension—the old process remained active with all its allocated memory. Only terminating both Shadowrocket and MacPacketTunnel properly restarted it. Afterward, the tunnel’s footprint dropped from 5.68 GB to just 5.5 MB, confirming that memory had accumulated inside the long-running extension.

Please fix this memory leak and ensure the packet-tunnel extension is properly terminated or cleaned up when Shadowrocket disconnects or restarts. The VPN functionality is useful, but this issue makes long-running use on macOS unreliable.
